sections.h2: Where are Calhoun County land records filed?
sections.html:
Calhoun County accepts land documents in one place only: the Marshall County Building at 315 West Green Street, home of the Clerk and Register of Deeds. The second office, at 161 East Michigan Avenue in Battle Creek, deals with circuit court filings and personal protection orders, so a deed taken there goes nowhere. Call the Marshall counter at 269-781-0718.

Title researchers and genealogists use the research room, open business days from 8 a.m. until 4:45 p.m., a quarter hour before the office itself closes. The Marshall building also issues marriage licenses, vital records and notary commissions, so expect a mixed crowd at the counter. A drop box at the west edge of the parking lot behind the County Building takes completed documents with payment enclosed. The county also provides an online land record search and a property alert tool.

Clerks do not give legal advice about completing a land record form, and the office stocks no blank forms. Questions go to a lawyer; the county suggests the State Bar of Michigan referral line, 1-800-968-0738, or Michigan Legal Help.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees at the Calhoun County office?
sections.html:
A flat $30 buys the recording of any document, long or short. The list the county gives includes deeds, mortgages, certified copies, lis pendens, timber, oil and gas leases, UCC filings, Land Division Act filings, discharges and terminations, and federal, state and employment security liens. Land record payments are taken as cash or check, nothing else.

  • Add $3 for each additional liber and page referenced on a discharge or assignment.
  • Pay $5 to the treasurer for the tax certification a warranty deed or land contract requires.
  • Copies cost $1 a page for real estate records, $2 for UCC filings, and at least $2 a page for plats.
  • Certification of a recorded instrument is $5.

The statute behind the base fee is MCL 600.2567: $30 to enter and record a document, with $3 added for each further instrument assigned or discharged.

sections.h2: Can I record a Calhoun County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, with one carve-out. Every document type can be e-recorded except those that require a real estate transfer tax valuation affidavit, which have to be mailed or brought to the Marshall counter. The process runs through a vendor: you scan and upload, the register reviews, and anything with errors comes back for correction before it is stamped and returned by electronic delivery.

Four vendors work with the county: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. Sign up as a customer with one of them; each offers demonstrations and training. Where a document needs tax certification, the system routes it to the County Treasurer's Office, so no separate trip is needed for the certificate.

sections.h2: What does the Marshall office check on a Calhoun County deed?
sections.html:
The county's posted checklist rests on MCL 565.201 and adds items that catch people who draft their own deeds.

  • Signatures in original ink, each with a typed or printed name below it that agrees with the notary block.
  • Street or post office addresses for grantees, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A Michigan acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary.
  • For any deed that names a survivor, a certified death certificate that was recorded earlier and is cited by liber and page.
  • Court orders bearing the court clerk's certification and seal.
  • A first line stating one recordable event, black type of 10 points or more on white 20-pound paper, and a 2 1/2 inch blank band above the first line of page one and 1/2 inch on the other edges.
  • The land's total value shown on the deed or in an attached valuation affidavit. The county bars the stock phrase "and other good and valuable consideration."
  • Any transfer tax exemption spelled out on the instrument, and a trust document recorded as a separate paper.

sections.h2: Who certifies taxes before a Calhoun County warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Calhoun County Treasurer does. Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts and any deed with a warranty covenant need the treasurer's certification before the register will take them, at $5. The treasurer's office shares the County Building at 315 West Green Street and is open Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to noon. Deed certification questions go to 269-781-0807.

MCL 211.135 is the source. The certificate must show that no tax liens or tax titles are held against the parcel and that taxes for the preceding five years are paid. A plain quitclaim without a warranty covenant falls outside it.

The same office collects delinquent real estate taxes for the county's 28 townships, cities and villages, so an owner who has fallen behind learns of it at this step. Clear the balance ahead of the closing date to keep the recording on schedule.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a Calhoun County sale?
sections.html:
Stack the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) on the state's $3.75 (MCL 207.525) and you get $4.30 for each $500 of value, with any remainder counted as one more block. The law counts a fraction of a block as a whole one, so a $162,800 home, the county's Census median, becomes 326 blocks instead of 325.6.

Owners selling a troubled property care most about three exemptions. A deed in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure on any mortgage is exempt under the state act, while the county act covers only government-backed loans. A court order that sets no price escapes both taxes. A transfer to a child or grandchild appears on the state list in MCL 207.526. Whatever you claim should be written on the instrument.

sections.h2: How big is Calhoun County, and who lives in its homes?
sections.html:
Calhoun County has 718 square miles of area, 706 of it land, centered on Battle Creek, the largest city, and Marshall, the seat. Albion and Springfield are the other cities. Athens, Burlington, Homer, Tekonsha and Union City are villages, and sixteen townships fill the rest. Established in 1829 and organized in 1833, the county is the core of the Battle Creek metropolitan area.

The Census Bureau estimates 133,408 residents for 2025 in 59,808 housing units. Owners live in 72.7% of homes, the typical owner-occupied value is $162,800, typical gross rent is $968, and the county has 53,333 households earning a median $63,177.

At that typical value, a sale triggers roughly $1,400 of transfer tax, and the rates are the same in every Michigan county.

faqs.q: What will I owe the Calhoun County recorder for a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document, paid in cash or by check. A discharge or assignment adds $3 per additional liber and page it references, and a warranty deed needs the $5 treasurer tax certification as well.

faqs.q: Will the Battle Creek office record my deed?
faqs.a: No. Land document recordings are filed only at the Marshall office, 315 West Green Street. Battle Creek handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available for Calhoun County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, through CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A document with a transfer tax valuation affidavit is the exception and must be mailed or delivered to Marshall.

faqs.q: What commonly gets a Calhoun County deed returned?
faqs.a: Typical reasons are a missing grantee address, no drafter name, signer names that disagree with the acknowledgment, no stated property value, and margins or type size outside the statute. The office returns rejected paper with the reasons checked off.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the Calhoun County transfer tax in a sale?
faqs.a: The statutes tax the written instrument and leave payment to the parties, so the purchase agreement governs. A $162,800 sale carries $1,401.80 in combined county and state tax.
